measurement.method: The kit's own overlay (NEW FPS / FRAME / P95 / GPU) plus the shim's STAT d3d9 lines, which are printed every 300 presented frames. Focus is held with Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled because the game pauses itself when the document loses activation.

root_causes: The translator computed fn.seh_restores in prepare() and never consulted it: the rule that emits recomp_seh_frame_leave for MOV FS:[0], reg was gated on fn.seh_sites, which is empty for the epilogue block body_004835cc because its prologue lives in another recovered block. Address 0x004835ef therefore emitted no leave, so fn_00481300 installed 845 SEH frames and retired none.

The runtime retire predicate was registration < ESP, which cannot fire for this MSVC epilogue shape: it loads the chain head from [ESP+0x1fc] into ECX and pops only part of the frame, leaving ESP below the registration.

stage_lock allocated a full-resource staging block on the first Lock and stage_unlock copied and freed it on the last, so a game that locks a dynamic buffer once per draw paid an allocation, two copies and a free per draw. gpu_after_unlock additionally marked the whole buffer dirty, so every draw re-uploaded the entire vertex or index buffer.
fixes: tools/recomp/translate.py: the MOV rule now consults fn.seh_restores with a seh_unproven_establishment guard so a body whose establishment could not be proven is not retired. Emissions of recomp_seh_frame_leave go from 6 to 563.

runtime/seh.cpp: frame liveness is decided by membership in the guest SEH chain, the same test recomp_seh_resume_frame already applied, with a bounded prune_unlinked_frames net (one pass every 1024 resumptions and only above 32 live frames). recomp_callback_depth() is hoisted out of the scan loop.

dx/d3d9.cpp and dx/com.h: the staging block survives the lock (stage_bytes) for vertex and index buffers only; a texture frees it on unlock so a second full image is not held per texture for the whole session. Unlock uploads only the locked range, widened outward to a four-byte multiple because the backend write offset must be aligned.
reverted_experiments: Implementing os_monotonic_ns with emscripten_get_now() instead of clock_gettime: _emscripten_get_now rose from 9.6% to 28.7% of the guest thread in the profile. Reverted on that direct measurement.

Reading the scheduler checkpoint clock once every 16 calls: first rejected on a comparison that was invalid because the two sides were sampled at different points of asset loading (frames 8101-9601 against 11101-12601). Re-measured with the stable protocol (settle 340 s, read the tail STAT reports) it gives 19.1 FPS against 18.6-19.6 without the change, so it is within noise and was dropped for adding scheduler latency without a measurable gain.

Lesson recorded for later rounds: frame rate figures are only comparable between runs that reach the same point of the scene, which is why the protocol settles 340 s and discards the loading-phase reports.
verified: The scene renders: final_scene.png and cur2_scene.png show the alley with CJ, the street, trees and the HUD, with no WebGPU validation warning and no abort in the page log.
The earlier BufferOffset (122454) is not a multiple of 4 WebGPU error introduced by narrowing the dirty range is gone after widening the range to a four-byte boundary.

The narrowed upload range is correct under moving geometry, which a static screenshot cannot show: holding w for 40 s produced 72 distinct view captures out of 72 samples, and mv1_after_move.png shows CJ out of the alley with the street billboard, palms, buildings, a parked car, the radar and the HUD, with no stale triangles. With the city in view the cost rises to 12.0-12.8 FPS at 1154-1249 draws per frame.
The SEH leak is closed on the shipped image: live_frames_max is 1, seh_frames and chain_visits read 0/s, and frames reports live=0 with enters_total=1550.
not_verified: Missions, vehicles, audio actually heard, saving and loading.
Stability beyond about 35 minutes of wall time.
Draw coverage across the whole city.
The 17.8 FPS figure is one static alley scene, not a traversal; the same street while walking measures 12.0-12.8 FPS. CAP 60 in the overlay is the kit's configured frame limit, not a measured cap.

remaining_profile.guest_thread: After both fixes the guest thread has no dominant cost: __pthread_cond_timedwait 13.6%, Emscripten invoke_* exception trampolines with get/getWasmTableEntry/wasm-to-js about 11%, clock reads about 9%, translated game code about 11%, D3D9 staging 3.9%, imports_dispatch 2.1%, printf_core 1.2%.
remaining_profile.not_done: Disabling C++ exception catching would remove the invoke_* wasm-to-JS-to-wasm trampolines, but interp.cpp relies on throw/catch for guest memory faults and the gain measured indirectly is about 2 FPS, so it was not attempted.
